verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's own CLI can return current TOTP codes: a runtime probe says `bw serve` exposes the vault as a local REST API that an agent can query for TOTP codes, and a hands-on user report says `bw list` printed current TOTP codes. The personal API key is documented as suitable for headless CLI authentication in automated workflows. Coverage is not complete, because no first-party doc in the pack documents a dedicated TOTP-retrieval command or endpoint, and the only hands-on evidence is an incidental bulk dump rather than a targeted fetch. missing for 10: first-party documentation of a specific TOTP-fetch CLI command or Vault Management API endpoint, end-to-end evidence of an agent completing a 2FA login with the fetched code, and independent corroboration of TOTP retrieval through `bw serve`.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can fetch a current TOTP code programmatically — via CLI or API — to complete a 2FA login inside an automated workflow

citations.quote: the CLI whose documented `bw serve` mode exposes the whole vault as a local RESTful API (Vault Management API) an agent can query for TOTP codes and items.
it listed everything including passwords and current totp codes in plaintext
Using the personal API key for CLI authentication is suitable for automated workflows
it automatically produces the time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs)
